clue.text: Mr Plod's handicap?

parts.note: Mr Plod is the comic village policeman of Enid Blyton's Noddy books, and a plodding policeman is nicknamed a flatfoot; the clue asks what affliction such a bobby suffers from

explanation.surface: A question about what holds back a slow-witted village bobby.
explanation.definitionFit: Policemen are slangily called flatfoots, so a fallen-arch condition is the joke ailment of the plodding constable.

clue.text: No cottage industry works rurally

parts.note: works is a noun for a plant, so this describes industrial plants set in the countryside, the opposite of small home crafts

explanation.surface: A remark that home crafts no longer operate in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive livestock units run like industrial works on farmland are the reverse of small cottage enterprises.

clue.text: A party almost in pieces

indicators.note: almost means the word party stops just short of its final letter

explanation.surface: A celebration that has nearly fallen to bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken apart is broken into separate pieces.

clue.text: He's under oath to exchange forenames

indicators.note: exchange signals the letters of forenames swapping places to form a new word

explanation.surface: A sworn witness is required to swap first names with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A freemason swears secret oaths on joining the fraternity of the Masonic lodge.

clue.text: Revelations of secret trips

definitions.meaning: exposures of someone's hidden sexuality or other concealed facts

explanation.surface: Disclosures about clandestine journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Outing someone exposes a secret, and short pleasure excursions are also called by this word.

clue.text: Coming from China, bird follows stormy sea

indicators.note: the bird is placed after the rearranged sea
a stormy sea is churned up, so its letters are churned too

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A gull-like bird from China trails a rough ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: China lies in the East, so things from there are eastern in origin.

clue.text: Canteen serving tuna — a fine ingredient

indicators.note: an ingredient sits inside a mixture, so the answer lies inside the words tuna a fine

explanation.surface: A cafeteria offers tuna dishes made with a quality component.
explanation.walkthrough: The NAAFI is the organisation running shops and canteens for British armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The NAAFI runs canteens and shops for the British services, and its name is used for the canteen itself.

clue.text: Fish eggs, fruit of the deep

definitions.meaning: the grape-like egg clusters laid by cuttlefish, though not true fish, go by this name
a whimsical reading: vine fruit growing under the ocean

explanation.surface: Roe described as a harvest from the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuttlefish egg clusters resemble bunches of grapes from the ocean, hence the name.

clue.text: Crack the thing

definitions.meaning: a network of fine cracks in a glaze or varnish, or the verb to produce them
the current fashion, as in 'it's all the thing', a short-lived enthusiasm

explanation.surface: An instruction to break some object.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazing is fine cracking on pottery glaze, and a passing fad is what everyone calls the thing just now.

clue.text: Grilled toast with the German dishes

indicators.note: food that is grilled is cooked and changed, so the word toast is reworked into new order

parts.note: das is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Toast cooked under the grill alongside some German food.
explanation.definitionFit: Tostadas are Mexican dishes of crisp fried tortillas topped with beans, meat and salad.

clue.text: Stirring porridge?

parts.note: stir and porridge are both British slang for jail and time served there, not a cook at the stove

explanation.surface: Someone mixing a pot of oatmeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir and porridge are British slang for prison and a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing porridge in stir is slang for serving a jail term, which is confinement in prison.

clue.text: Seat of Empire, once

definitions.meaning: a low upholstered seat or footstool without a back
belonging to the former Turkish empire ruled from Constantinople

explanation.surface: A grand phrase for the capital that once ruled an empire.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is a padded backless couch, and the Ottoman Empire was the Turkish state that ended in 1922.

clue.text: Record current weight produces satirical comment

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
I is the symbol for electric current
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Logging the electricity and mass results in a witty jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short pointed saying, often satirical in tone.

clue.text: American soprano shows drawing power

parts.note: a Yank is informal for an American
S is the musical abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A US singer proves she can pull in the crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to pull sharply, so one who yanks shows a capacity for drawing or tugging.

clue.text: Fashion that's had its day?

parts.note: not an outdated style but clothing worn once the day is over, at bedtime

explanation.surface: A remark about a style that has gone out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nightdresses are clothes worn after the day is done.

clue.text: Smooth novelist with her composition

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin
a paper is a written essay or composition

explanation.surface: A suave writer accompanied by something she wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smooth' looks like an adjective describing the novelist, but it is a verb: what you do with this abrasive sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: To sandpaper wood is to rub it smooth with abrasive paper.

clue.text: One who lined shabby stall with pine

indicators.note: shabby suggests something knocked about, so the letters of stall and pine are rearranged

explanation.surface: A carpenter clad a worn-out market stand in pine boards.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful reading: someone who fits panels, lining a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel lines a wall, so one who panels is jokingly a panellist, normally a member of a panel.

clue.text: Place for mixing granite with sodium

indicators.note: the word granite is put in for mixing, so its letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium

explanation.surface: A site where rock is blended with a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a country in South America, and so a place.

clue.text: Nice tax reform? No, its not nice

indicators.note: reform means to form again, so the letters of Nice and tax are reshaped

explanation.surface: A question whether a French tax overhaul in Nice is precise.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice in the definition means precise, as in a nice distinction, not pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: One old sense of nice is exact or finely precise, so lacking that is being imprecise.

clue.text: Where to find a fool in Belgium

definitions.text: Where to find a fool in Belgium

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, the form of a used before a vowel sound
a twerp is a silly person

explanation.surface: A question about locating an idiot in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major port city in Belgium.

clue.text: Homes established in a partnership

indicators.note: the abbreviation for established is placed in the middle of the partnership letters

parts.note: in bridge, North and South play as a partnership, N S

explanation.surface: Households founded within a joint business.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is played by two pairs, North-South against East-West, so a partnership can be NS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nests are the homes birds build, and by extension any snug dwelling.

clue.text: Is it staged for idol worshippers?

definitions.text: Is it staged for idol worshippers?

parts.words: Is it staged for idol worshippers?
parts.note: fans adoring a handsome screen star call him a ... idol, so the afternoon show is put on for those who idolise him

explanation.surface: A question whether a show is put on for fans of a heart-throb.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon theatre performance gave its name to the matinee idol, a star adored by female fans.

clue.text: Even good ground produced this area

indicators.note: ground means crushed and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Level fertile soil yielded crops in this region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as soil but is the anagram signal, as in ground coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: The Negev is the desert region of southern Israel, the area this clue points to.

clue.text: Author who did not like translation

indicators.note: a translation turns words into something else, so these letters are rendered in a new order

explanation.surface: A writer who disliked having his work put into other languages.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: this author was a philologist famously fussy about translations of his books.
explanation.definitionFit: J R R Tolkien was the English author of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.

clue.text: Half of duumvirate up in arms

indicators.note: half of the word means only its second five letters are taken

explanation.surface: One of two joint rulers is in revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: A duumvirate is rule by two people, so half of it is fittingly half the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up in arms is an idiom for being furious or protesting angrily.

clue.text: Barge led out on the Danube here

definitions.text: Barge led out on the Danube here

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of barge and led are rearranged

explanation.surface: A river vessel is guided out along the Danube at this city.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade, capital of Serbia, stands where the Sava meets the Danube, a natural port for barges.

clue.text: Picture me pocketing silver after one

indicators.note: the remainder is placed after the numeral for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word me puts the silver symbol into its pocket, around it

parts.note: taken as written
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A photo of myself holding cash, taken after one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness of something.

clue.text: One who hopes to pay well

definitions.text: One who hopes to pay well

parts.words: One who hopes to pay well
parts.note: a sick person hopes to get well, and one who pays for treatment outside the free health service hopes the fee brings recovery

explanation.surface: Someone who wants to be generous with money.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain most care is free on the NHS; a fee-paying patient goes private.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient paying for medical care outside the state health service hopes the money will make them well.
